title: One-Hand Push Pass Technique
description: Players learn the one-hand push pass from the shooting pocket, the quickest pass in basketball, first stationary and then off the dribble.

content.objective: Pass quickly with either hand from the pocket, without bringing the ball to the chest.
content.setup: Partners five metres apart, one ball per pair.
content.organization: Pairs; switch hands after ten passes.
instructions: Hold the ball at the right hip (shooting pocket) with the left hand on the side.
Push it to the partner with the right hand, snapping the wrist, thumb down.
Partner catches and returns with the same hand.
After ten, switch to the left hand.
Progress to a one-hand push pass straight off a live dribble.
coachingPoints: The pass comes from the hip, not the chest.
Wrist snap and follow-through to the target.
Step with the same-side foot to add power.
commonMistakes: Bringing the ball to the chest first (slow, readable).
Pushing with the arm only, without a wrist snap.
content.safety: Pairs spaced so errant passes roll into open court.
progressions: Pass off the dribble in one motion.
Pass across the body to the opposite side.
regressions: Two-hand chest passes from the hip.
successCriteria: Ten accurate passes with each hand.
Ball never comes up to the chest.
content.gameApplication: The one-hand pass is how guards hit shooters and cutters without giving the defense time to react.
